prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, through bifunctional PROTAC degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of molecular-glue degraders, which direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: I keep B019 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The shared principle is chemically induced proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, so that a small molecule removes a protein instead of inhibiting it. That is a new capability, it reaches targets without a conventional pocket, and it has been reproduced by many independent laboratories with structural support from ternary-complex crystal structures. Round 1 showed that this is the only ballot where the disagreement is about one name rather than about the discovery: five members explicitly back it, and Somfai, Brzezinski and Sparr each list it as an alternative. Handa belongs in the trio because cereblon explains how thalidomide-type drugs act and shows that PROTACs and glues are two routes to the same E3-hijacking logic. That makes the citation a statement of principle that can be explained to a broad audience, in the spirit of what the committee said in 2024 and 2025 about opening up unforeseen possibilities.
statement.case_against: The reservations stand and I do not want them smoothed over. As far as I know no degrader is approved, and I cannot verify that from the files, so the case rests on mechanism, replication and late-stage trials rather than a delivered medicine. Ternary-complex cooperativity is still only partly quantified. Credit is crowded: Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim all have real claims, and a three-name cap forces a line between the PROTAC and glue strands. A single citation covering both may be read as two discoveries compressed into one. I also correct my round-1 wording: B019 was not a top-four placement for all eight members, since Sparr ranked it sixth and Brzezinski seventh. The breadth of support is real but narrower than I said, and I rely on the science, not the count.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a PROTAC-only citation, arguing that adding Handa makes a two-strand prize that is hard to state in one sentence and that Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work are intrinsic to rational design.
responses.response: This is the decisive question for the trio and I have weighed it seriously. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are what made PROTACs drug-like and quantitative, and if the committee chooses a PROTAC-only citation he is the right third name. My difficulty is that a PROTAC-only citation leaves the best-established mechanistic result in the field, the cereblon identification that explains the thalidomide class, outside the prize, and Somfai predicted exactly this objection. I do not accept that a citation naming induced proximity through E3 recruitment is a two-sentence prize. Ciulli's contribution refines how to design a PROTAC, whereas Handa's discovery added a second, independently grounded route to the same principle. I keep Handa, and I record that Ciulli is the natural choice if the committee prefers the narrower story.

responses.point: Somfai asks what is chemically new in degraders, says recognition may be premature without an approved PROTAC, and warns that the PROTAC and cereblon stories should not be merged under one citation without a clear reason.
responses.response: The chemically new element is not a reaction but a design principle: a bifunctional or glue molecule creates a neo-interaction, so that ligand, linker and surface chemistry decide whether an E3 ligase acts on a chosen target. That is the reason I do not see this as a second prize for an old idea, which is the objection I would raise against B034 given the 2010 cross-coupling prize. My clear reason for one citation is that cereblon is the E3 ligase through which both thalidomide-type glues and the most widely used PROTACs act, so the strands share a mechanism. On timing I agree with you more than Aqvist does. I would still not defer, because the Nobel standard has been a demonstrated principle with independent confirmation, but approval status is the fact I most want checked before final ballots.

responses.point: Sparr prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045) with Cullis, Hope and Anderson, and argues that approved products and real-world safety data make it more mature than B019, while flagging crowded credit and the overlap with Medicine 2023.
responses.response: The self-assembly chemistry is real, and pKa-tuned lipids with phase behaviour that releases cargo are a genuine design principle, so I do not dismiss it. I also respect that you name your own field bias and the overlap with Medicine 2023. My two reasons for keeping it behind B019 are attribution and novelty of the discovery being named. Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer each have a distinct step, and your trio leaves out Madden, whom Aili and you both regard as central to the early lipid work. I also still think the committee would be asked to explain a second recognition of the mRNA delivery story. If the committee decides maturity must include an approved product, B045 is the strongest alternative on that axis and I take that argument seriously.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers long-range protein electron transfer (B055) with Gray and Winkler for mechanistic depth and a clean two-name attribution, and ranked B019 seventh because of missing approval and the separate PROTAC and glue strands.
responses.response: I agree that B055 has the cleanest attribution on the list and that the physical-chemistry evidence is quantitative and reproduced, which appeals to my own physicist's preferences. I cannot get past the 1992 Marcus prize, which you acknowledge yourself: the distance-dependent tunnelling picture looks like the experimental confirmation of recognised theory, and the priority of Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic is unresolved. You also said that B019 is your alternative if attribution and maturity questions are answered. My answer on attribution is Handa as the explicit link between the strands, and on maturity the evidence is mechanism and independent replication, with approval to be verified. If you can show that Gray and Winkler's contribution is a distinct discovery rather than the experimental half of the Marcus prize, I would listen, but I do not see that yet.

uncertainties: Whether any PROTAC or comparable degrader has regulatory approval, which I have not verified from the files and which would settle my maturity concern.
Whether the committee will accept a trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa as one achievement, or will prefer Ciulli as the third name for a PROTAC-only citation.
Whether Sakamoto's first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies is a priority claim that outweighs one of the named trio; the files do not settle it.
Whether nanopore sensing (B002) could be given a defensible three-name attribution, given Bayley's role in engineered pores.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B019 or my alternatives B002 and B018. I am a physicist at Lund and share an institution with committee members Somfai and Sparr, but none of the candidates is a colleague, collaborator or Lund affiliate. No disclosure has changed since round 1, and I regard none as a basis for recusal.
